**Clarence James Brown III** (born January 5, 1959) is an American actor. Prolific in film and television since the 1980s, Brown is often cast in villainous and authoritative roles.

His film roles include Rawhide in _[The Adventures of Buckaroo Banzai Across the 8th Dimension](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Adventures\_of\_Buckaroo\_Banzai\_Across\_the\_8th\_Dimension "The Adventures of Buckaroo Banzai Across the 8th Dimension")_ (1984), [Frankenstein's monster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frankenstein's_monster "Frankenstein's monster") in _[The Bride](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Bride\_(1985\_film) "The Bride (1985 film)")_ (1985), [the Kurgan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Kurgan "The Kurgan") in _[Highlander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Highlander\_(film) "Highlander (film)")_ (1986), Sheriff Gus Gilbert in _[Pet Sematary Two](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pet\_Sematary\_Two "Pet Sematary Two")_ (1992), Capt. Byron Hadley in _[The Shawshank Redemption](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Shawshank\_Redemption "The Shawshank Redemption")_ (1994), Sgt. Charles Zim in _[Starship Troopers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starship\_Troopers\_(film) "Starship Troopers (film)")_ (1997), Stanley Thomas in _[Promising Young Woman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Promising\_Young\_Woman "Promising Young Woman")_ (2020), and the Harbinger in _[John Wick: Chapter 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John\_Wick:\_Chapter\_4 "John Wick: Chapter 4")_ (2023). Brown has voiced [Lex Luthor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lex_Luthor "Lex Luthor") in various [DC Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DC_Comics "DC Comics") animated media since 1996 and [Mr. Krabs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr._Krabs "Mr. Krabs") on _[SpongeBob SquarePants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpongeBob\_SquarePants "SpongeBob SquarePants")_ since 1999. His other voice roles include [Long Feng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Avatar:_The_Last_Airbender_characters#Earth_Kingdom "List of Avatar: The Last Airbender characters") in _[Avatar: The Last Airbender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avatar:\_The\_Last\_Airbender "Avatar: The Last Airbender")_ (2006), [Savage Opress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savage_Opress "Savage Opress") in _[Star Wars: The Clone Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Wars:\_The\_Clone\_Wars "Star Wars: The Clone Wars")_ (2011–2013), [Surtur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surtur_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe) "Surtur (Marvel Cinematic Universe)") in _[Thor: Ragnarok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thor:\_Ragnarok "Thor: Ragnarok")_ (2017) and General Kregg in _[Invincible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invincible\_(TV\_series) "Invincible (TV series)")_ (2021–2026). In video games, he voiced [Doctor Neo Cortex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Neo_Cortex "Doctor Neo Cortex") and Uka Uka in the _[Crash Bandicoot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crash\_Bandicoot "Crash Bandicoot")_ franchise (1997–2003) and performed the motion capture and voice of Hank Anderson in _[Detroit: Become Human](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit:\_Become\_Human "Detroit: Become Human")_ (2018).

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Clancy_Brown&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Clarence James Brown III was born on January 5, 1959,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clancy_Brown#cite_note-1) in [Urbana, Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urbana,_Ohio "Urbana, Ohio"),[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clancy_Brown#cite_note-TVG-2) and had an older sister, Beth, who died in 1964. Their mother, Joyce Helen (née Eldridge), was a conductor, composer and concert pianist. The siblings' father, [Clarence J. "Bud" Brown Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bud_Brown_(politician) "Bud Brown (politician)"),[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clancy_Brown#cite_note-3) was a newspaper publisher who helped manage the [Brown Publishing Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brown_Publishing_Company "Brown Publishing Company"), the family-owned newspaper business started by Clancy's grandfather, Congressman [Clarence J. Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clarence_J._Brown "Clarence J. Brown"). From 1965 to 1983, Bud Brown also served as a congressman, in the same seat as his own father, and later as [Chairman of the Board](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chairman_of_the_Board "Chairman of the Board") of Brown Publishing.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clancy_Brown#cite_note-4) The family continued to operate the business until 2010.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Brown graduated from [St. Albans School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Albans_School_(Washington,_D.C.) "St. Albans School (Washington, D.C.)") in [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C."), and [Northwestern University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northwestern_University "Northwestern University").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clancy_Brown#cite_note-MSN-5) At St. Albans, Brown performed the role of Deputy Governor [Thomas Danforth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Danforth "Thomas Danforth") in _[The Crucible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Crucible "The Crucible")_.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clancy_Brown#cite_note-6)

### Live-action performances

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Clancy_Brown&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Live-action performances")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/33/Clancy_Brown.jpg/250px-Clancy_Brown.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Clancy_Brown.jpg)

Brown in 2008

In Brown's first mainstream film, he was cast as Viking Lofgren alongside Sean Penn in the 1983 crime drama _[Bad Boys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad\_Boys\_(1983\_film) "Bad Boys (1983 film)")_. He followed up as the sadistic [Kurgan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurgan_(Highlander) "Kurgan (Highlander)") in the 1986 film _[Highlander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Highlander\_(film) "Highlander (film)")_, which failed in theaters but had more success on home video. Other eighties roles included Army mercenary Larry McRose in [Walter Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Hill "Walter Hill")'s _[Extreme Prejudice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extreme\_Prejudice\_(film) "Extreme Prejudice (film)")_, killer Steve in [Roger Spottiswoode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Spottiswoode "Roger Spottiswoode")'s _[Shoot to Kill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoot\_to\_Kill\_(1988\_film) "Shoot to Kill (1988 film)")_ and Detective Nick Mann in [Kathryn Bigelow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kathryn_Bigelow "Kathryn Bigelow")'s _[Blue Steel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue\_Steel\_(1990\_film) "Blue Steel (1990 film)")_.

Brown has played prison officers in three films dealing with miscarriages of justice: the tyrannical Captain Byron Hadley in _[The Shawshank Redemption](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Shawshank\_Redemption "The Shawshank Redemption")_, the sympathetic Lt. Jimmy Williams in _[The Hurricane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hurricane\_(1999\_film) "The Hurricane (1999 film)")_, and Lt. McMannis in _[Last Light](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Last\_Light\_(film) "Last Light (film)")_. In 2001, he played a magical character credited as 'The granter of wishes' in the Hallmark version of _[Snow White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snow\_White:\_The\_Fairest\_of\_Them\_All "Snow White: The Fairest of Them All")_. In 2007, he played the Viking leader opposite [Karl Urban](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl_Urban "Karl Urban") in _[Pathfinder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathfinder\_(2007\_film) "Pathfinder (2007 film)")_.

He starred in several independent films in 2008: _[The Burrowers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Burrowers "The Burrowers")_, screened at the [Toronto International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto_International_Film_Festival "Toronto International Film Festival") in 2008, and released in the United States on DVD in April 2009, and _The Twenty_. He appeared in [Steven Soderbergh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Soderbergh "Steven Soderbergh")'s 2009 film _[The Informant!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Informant! "The Informant!")_ opposite [Matt Damon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Damon "Matt Damon") in which he played an attorney. He also portrayed Alan Smith in [Samuel Bayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_Bayer "Samuel Bayer")'s 2010 remake of the horror film _[A Nightmare on Elm Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Nightmare\_on\_Elm\_Street\_(2010\_film) "A Nightmare on Elm Street (2010 film)")_.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clancy_Brown#cite_note-:0-7) In 2011, he appeared in _[Cowboys & Aliens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowboys\_&\_Aliens "Cowboys & Aliens")_ (directed by [Jon Favreau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Favreau "Jon Favreau")) with [Daniel Craig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Craig "Daniel Craig"), [Harrison Ford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrison_Ford "Harrison Ford") and [Olivia Wilde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olivia_Wilde "Olivia Wilde"). He was cast as the voice of _[The Goon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Goon "The Goon")_ in the animated [feature film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Goon_(film) "The Goon (film)"). He also starred as Albert Marconi in the [film adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Dies_at_the_End_(film) "John Dies at the End (film)") of the David Wong [novel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Novel "Novel")_[John Dies at the End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John\_Dies\_at\_the\_End "John Dies at the End")_, directed by [Don Coscarelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Coscarelli "Don Coscarelli").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clancy_Brown#cite_note-8)

Brown was a series regular on the science fiction series _[Earth 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth\_2\_(TV\_series) "Earth 2 (TV series)")_ from 1994 to 1995, playing the role of John Danziger. Brown was notable as the sinister preacher [Brother Justin Crowe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brother_Justin_Crowe "Brother Justin Crowe") in the HBO series _[Carnivàle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carniv%C3%A0le "Carnivàle")_. Though the series only ran for two seasons, _Carnivàle_ has attained a cult popularity and his performance was applauded by critics for showcasing a new side to his acting talents. He also starred in the [Showtime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Showtime_(TV_network) "Showtime (TV network)") production _In the Company of Spies_ and the HBO film _[Cast a Deadly Spell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cast\_a\_Deadly\_Spell "Cast a Deadly Spell")_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clancy_Brown#cite_note-NYT-9) As conservative United States Attorney General Jock Jeffcoat, he was one of the primary antagonists in seasons three and four of the Showtime series _[Billions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billions\_(TV\_series) "Billions (TV series)")._[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clancy_Brown#cite_note-10)

He has also made many guest appearances on various television series including _[ER](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ER\_(TV\_series) "ER (TV series)")_, the _[Star Trek: Enterprise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Trek:\_Enterprise "Star Trek: Enterprise")_ episode "[Desert Crossing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desert_Crossing "Desert Crossing")" as Zobral, _[Lost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lost\_(2004\_TV\_series) "Lost (2004 TV series)")_ as [Kelvin Joe Inman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Characters_of_Lost#Dharma_Initiative_members "Characters of Lost"), and former baseball player (and investment scam mark) Rudy Blue on _[The Riches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Riches "The Riches")_. Brown also appeared as the frontiersman [Simon Kenton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Kenton "Simon Kenton"), the key to America's westward expansion, in the 2000 [Kentucky Educational Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky_Educational_Television "Kentucky Educational Television") production "A Walk with Simon Kenton". Kenton resembled Brown in stature and is buried in Brown's hometown. Brown most recently appeared as Hart Sterling, founding partner of fictional law firm Sterling, Huddle, Oppenheim & Craft in [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company")'s _[The Deep End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Deep\_End\_(2010\_TV\_series) "The Deep End (2010 TV series)")_. He also guest starred on the _[Leverage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leverage\_(American\_TV\_series) "Leverage (American TV series)")_ series episode "The Gone Fishin Job" and on _[The Dukes of Hazzard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Dukes\_of\_Hazzard "The Dukes of Hazzard")_ sixth-season episode "Too Many Roscos". He appeared on The CW's TV production of _[The Flash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Flash\_(2014\_TV\_series) "The Flash (2014 TV series)")_ in the recurring guest-star role of [General Wade Eiling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Wade_Eiling "General Wade Eiling"). He has also portrayed [Ray Schoonover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Schoonover_(comics) "Ray Schoonover (comics)") in the _[Daredevil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daredevil\_(TV\_series) "Daredevil (TV series)")_ episodes "[Guilty as Sin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guilty_as_Sin_(Daredevil_episode) "Guilty as Sin (Daredevil episode)")" and "[The Dark at the End of the Tunnel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dark_at_the_End_of_the_Tunnel "The Dark at the End of the Tunnel")" and _[The Punisher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Punisher\_(TV\_series) "The Punisher (TV series)")_ episode "[Kandahar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kandahar_(The_Punisher) "Kandahar (The Punisher)")". He played Sheriff Joe Corbin in _Sleepy Hollow_. In January 2021, it was announced Brown had been cast in Showtime's _[Dexter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dexter\_(TV\_series) "Dexter (TV series)")_ revival _[Dexter: New Blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dexter:\_New\_Blood "Dexter: New Blood")_ with a leading role as Kurt Caldwell.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clancy_Brown#cite_note-11) In 2022, Brown joined the cast of _[The Boys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Boys\_(TV\_series) "The Boys (TV series)")_ spin-off series _[Gen V](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gen\_V "Gen V")_ as Richard "Rich Brink" Brinkerhoff.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clancy_Brown#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clancy_Brown#cite_note-13) In 2025, Brown was cast as Big Hank Hickman in The CW’s series _[Good Cop/Bad Cop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good\_Cop/Bad\_Cop "Good Cop/Bad Cop")_.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clancy_Brown#cite_note-14)

#### DC Comics media

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Clancy_Brown&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: DC Comics media")]

Brown is well known for voicing the villainous [Lex Luthor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lex_Luthor "Lex Luthor") in various animated media since 1996. He first voiced Luthor in the [DC Animated Universe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DC_Animated_Universe "DC Animated Universe") (DCAU), starting with _[Superman: The Animated Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superman:\_The\_Animated\_Series "Superman: The Animated Series")_ (where he had originally auditioned for the role of [Superman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superman "Superman")) and reprised his role in the subsequent animated series _[Justice League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justice\_League\_(TV\_series) "Justice League (TV series)")_ and _[Justice League Unlimited](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justice\_League\_Unlimited "Justice League Unlimited")_. He also voiced the character in the video game _[Superman: Shadow of Apokolips](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superman:\_Shadow\_of\_Apokolips "Superman: Shadow of Apokolips")_ as well as _[The Batman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Batman\_(TV\_series) "The Batman (TV series)")_ cartoon series. Brown later again played Luthor in the 2009 animated film _[Superman/Batman: Public Enemies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superman/Batman:\_Public\_Enemies "Superman/Batman: Public Enemies")_. He also voiced a character under the name Rohtul (which is Luthor spelled backwards) in _[Batman: Brave and the Bold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batman:\_Brave\_and\_the\_Bold "Batman: Brave and the Bold")_ (while [Kevin Michael Richardson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Michael_Richardson "Kevin Michael Richardson") provided the voice of the actual character). Brown once again voiced Lex in the video games _[Lego Batman 2: DC Super Heroes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lego\_Batman\_2:\_DC\_Super\_Heroes "Lego Batman 2: DC Super Heroes")_, _[Lego Batman 3: Beyond Gotham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lego\_Batman\_3:\_Beyond\_Gotham "Lego Batman 3: Beyond Gotham")_ and _[Lego DC Super-Villains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lego\_DC\_Super-Villains "Lego DC Super-Villains")_. From all these vocal appearances, Brown has played Lex Luthor longer than any other actor in history, including his own _Justice League_ co-star [Michael Rosenbaum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Rosenbaum "Michael Rosenbaum") (in _[Smallville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smallville "Smallville")_).

Brown is also known for his voice work as villains in various [DC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DC_Comics "DC Comics") animated series, films, television shows, and video games: Charlie "Big Time" Bigelow on _[Batman Beyond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batman\_Beyond "Batman Beyond")_, [Trident](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trident_(DC_Comics) "Trident (DC Comics)") on _[Teen Titans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teen\_Titans\_(TV\_series) "Teen Titans (TV series)")_, [Mr. Freeze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr._Freeze "Mr. Freeze") and [Bane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bane_(DC_Comics) "Bane (DC Comics)") on _[The Batman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Batman\_(TV\_series) "The Batman (TV series)")_, [Per Degaton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Per_Degaton "Per Degaton") in _[Batman: The Brave and the Bold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batman:\_The\_Brave\_and\_the\_Bold "Batman: The Brave and the Bold")_, [Parallax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parallax_(character) "Parallax (character)") in the live-action _[Green Lantern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green\_Lantern\_(film) "Green Lantern (film)")_ film, [King Faraday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Faraday "King Faraday") in _[Young Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young\_Justice\_(TV\_series) "Young Justice (TV series)")_, and Zartok in _[Green Lantern: The Animated Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green\_Lantern:\_The\_Animated\_Series "Green Lantern: The Animated Series")_. He appeared on The CW's _[The Flash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Flash\_(2014\_TV\_series) "The Flash (2014 TV series)")_ recurring in the first season as [General Wade Eiling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Wade_Eiling "General Wade Eiling"), and on HBO's _[The Penguin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Penguin\_(TV\_series) "The Penguin (TV series)")_ as [Sal Maroni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sal_Maroni "Sal Maroni").

## Activism

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Clancy_Brown&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Activism")]

On March 30, 2012, the [Screen Actors Guild](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild "Screen Actors Guild") (SAG) and the [American Federation of Television and Radio Artists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Federation_of_Television_and_Radio_Artists "American Federation of Television and Radio Artists") (AFTRA) completed a merger of equals forming a new union [SAG-AFTRA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAG-AFTRA "SAG-AFTRA"). As a result of this merger, a group of actors including Brown, fellow voice actors [Michael Bell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bell_(actor) "Michael Bell (actor)"), [Wendy Schaal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wendy_Schaal "Wendy Schaal"), Schaal's former stepmother [Valerie Harper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valerie_Harper "Valerie Harper"), and other actors including former SAG President [Edward Asner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Asner "Edward Asner"), [Martin Sheen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Sheen "Martin Sheen"), [Ed Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Harris "Ed Harris"), and [Nancy Sinatra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Sinatra "Nancy Sinatra") immediately sued against the current SAG President [Ken Howard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Howard "Ken Howard") and several SAG Vice Presidents to overturn the merger and separate the (now merged) two unions because of their claims that the election was improper.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clancy_Brown#cite_note-19) The plaintiffs dropped their lawsuit several months later.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clancy_Brown#cite_note-20)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Clancy_Brown&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Brown has been married to Jeanne Johnson since 1993.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clancy_Brown#cite_note-Empire-21) They have two children.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clancy_Brown#cite_note-Empire-21)

Brown is involved in charity organizations, supporting the Beth Brown Memorial Fund named after his late sister, which offers scholarships to students who want to study pediatric healthcare.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clancy_Brown#cite_note-22) In 1999 he spearheaded a charity campaign to support [J. Madison Wright](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._Madison_Wright_Morris "J. Madison Wright Morris"), his on-screen daughter from _Earth 2_, who needed a heart transplant.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clancy_Brown#cite_note-23) He has also given back to his Alma mater the Northwestern University through benefit performances.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clancy_Brown#cite_note-24)

In a 2023 interview with [NPR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NPR "NPR"), Brown said that he came from a "very long legacy of [Republican ideology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)") - back when they _had_ an ideology." His father, Bud Brown, had passed from [COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19") complications the previous year.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clancy_Brown#cite_note-25)

**Clarence James Brown III** (born January 5, 1959) is an American actor. Prolific in film and television since the 1980s, Brown is often cast in villainous and authoritative roles.

His film roles include Rawhide in _[The Adventures of Buckaroo Banzai Across the 8th Dimension](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Adventures\_of\_Buckaroo\_Banzai\_Across\_the\_8th\_Dimension "The Adventures of Buckaroo Banzai Across the 8th Dimension")_ (1984), [Frankenstein's monster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frankenstein's_monster "Frankenstein's monster") in _[The Bride](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Bride\_(1985\_film) "The Bride (1985 film)")_ (1985), [the Kurgan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Kurgan "The Kurgan") in _[Highlander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Highlander\_(film) "Highlander (film)")_ (1986), Sheriff Gus Gilbert in _[Pet Sematary Two](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pet\_Sematary\_Two "Pet Sematary Two")_ (1992), Capt. Byron Hadley in _[The Shawshank Redemption](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Shawshank\_Redemption "The Shawshank Redemption")_ (1994), Sgt. Charles Zim in _[Starship Troopers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starship\_Troopers\_(film) "Starship Troopers (film)")_ (1997), Stanley Thomas in _[Promising Young Woman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Promising\_Young\_Woman "Promising Young Woman")_ (2020), and the Harbinger in _[John Wick: Chapter 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John\_Wick:\_Chapter\_4 "John Wick: Chapter 4")_ (2023). On television, he has played Brother Justin Crowe on the [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO") series _[Carnivàle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carniv%C3%A0le "Carnivàle")_ (2003–2005), Waylon "Jock" Jeffcoat on the [Showtime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Showtime_(TV_network) "Showtime (TV network)") series _[Billions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billions\_(TV\_series) "Billions (TV series)")_ (2018–2019, 2023), Kurt Caldwell on the Showtime series _[Dexter: New Blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dexter:\_New\_Blood "Dexter: New Blood")_ (2021–2022), and [Sal Maroni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sal_Maroni "Sal Maroni") in _[The Penguin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Penguin\_(TV\_series) "The Penguin (TV series)")_ (2024).

Brown has voiced [Lex Luthor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lex_Luthor "Lex Luthor") in various [DC Comics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DC_Comics "DC Comics") animated media since 1996 and [Mr. Krabs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr._Krabs "Mr. Krabs") on _[SpongeBob SquarePants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpongeBob\_SquarePants "SpongeBob SquarePants")_ since 1999. His other voice roles include [Long Feng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Avatar:_The_Last_Airbender_characters#Earth_Kingdom "List of Avatar: The Last Airbender characters") in _[Avatar: The Last Airbender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avatar:\_The\_Last\_Airbender "Avatar: The Last Airbender")_ (2006), [Savage Opress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savage_Opress "Savage Opress") in _[Star Wars: The Clone Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Wars:\_The\_Clone\_Wars "Star Wars: The Clone Wars")_ (2011–2013), [Surtur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surtur_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe) "Surtur (Marvel Cinematic Universe)") in _[Thor: Ragnarok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thor:\_Ragnarok "Thor: Ragnarok")_ (2017) and General Kregg in _[Invincible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invincible\_(TV\_series) "Invincible (TV series)")_ (2021–2026). In video games, he voiced [Doctor Neo Cortex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Neo_Cortex "Doctor Neo Cortex") and Uka Uka in the _[Crash Bandicoot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crash\_Bandicoot "Crash Bandicoot")_ franchise (1997–2003) and performed the motion capture and voice of Hank Anderson in _[Detroit: Become Human](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit:\_Become\_Human "Detroit: Become Human")_ (2018).

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Clancy_Brown&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Clarence James Brown III was born on January 5, 1959,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clancy_Brown#cite_note-1) in [Urbana, Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urbana,_Ohio "Urbana, Ohio"),[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clancy_Brown#cite_note-TVG-2) and had an older sister, Beth, who died in 1964. Their mother, Joyce Helen (née Eldridge), was a conductor, composer and concert pianist. The siblings' father, [Clarence J. "Bud" Brown Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bud_Brown_(politician) "Bud Brown (politician)"),[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clancy_Brown#cite_note-3) was a newspaper publisher who helped manage the [Brown Publishing Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brown_Publishing_Company "Brown Publishing Company"), the family-owned newspaper business started by Clancy's grandfather, Congressman [Clarence J. Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clarence_J._Brown "Clarence J. Brown"). From 1965 to 1983, Bud Brown also served as a congressman, in the same seat as his own father, and later as [Chairman of the Board](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chairman_of_the_Board "Chairman of the Board") of Brown Publishing.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clancy_Brown#cite_note-4) The family continued to operate the business until 2010.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Brown graduated from [St. Albans School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Albans_School_(Washington,_D.C.) "St. Albans School (Washington, D.C.)") in [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C."), and [Northwestern University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northwestern_University "Northwestern University").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clancy_Brown#cite_note-MSN-5) At St. Albans, Brown performed the role of Deputy Governor [Thomas Danforth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Danforth "Thomas Danforth") in _[The Crucible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Crucible "The Crucible")_.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clancy_Brown#cite_note-6)

### Live-action performances

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Clancy_Brown&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Live-action performances")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/33/Clancy_Brown.jpg/250px-Clancy_Brown.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Clancy_Brown.jpg)

Brown in 2008

In Brown's first mainstream film, he was cast as Viking Lofgren alongside Sean Penn in the 1983 crime drama _[Bad Boys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad\_Boys\_(1983\_film) "Bad Boys (1983 film)")_. He followed up as the sadistic [Kurgan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurgan_(Highlander) "Kurgan (Highlander)") in the 1986 film _[Highlander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Highlander\_(film) "Highlander (film)")_, which failed in theaters but had more success on home video. Other eighties roles included Army mercenary Larry McRose in [Walter Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walter_Hill "Walter Hill")'s _[Extreme Prejudice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extreme\_Prejudice\_(film) "Extreme Prejudice (film)")_, killer Steve in [Roger Spottiswoode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Spottiswoode "Roger Spottiswoode")'s _[Shoot to Kill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoot\_to\_Kill\_(1988\_film) "Shoot to Kill (1988 film)")_ and Detective Nick Mann in [Kathryn Bigelow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kathryn_Bigelow "Kathryn Bigelow")'s _[Blue Steel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue\_Steel\_(1990\_film) "Blue Steel (1990 film)")_.

#### DC Comics media

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Clancy_Brown&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: DC Comics media")]

Brown is well known for voicing the villainous [Lex Luthor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lex_Luthor "Lex Luthor") in various animated media since 1996. He first voiced Luthor in the [DC Animated Universe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DC_Animated_Universe "DC Animated Universe") (DCAU), starting with _[Superman: The Animated Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superman:\_The\_Animated\_Series "Superman: The Animated Series")_ (where he had originally auditioned for the role of [Superman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superman "Superman")) and reprised his role in the subsequent animated series _[Justice League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justice\_League\_(TV\_series) "Justice League (TV series)")_ and _[Justice League Unlimited](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justice\_League\_Unlimited "Justice League Unlimited")_. He also voiced the character in the video game _[Superman: Shadow of Apokolips](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superman:\_Shadow\_of\_Apokolips "Superman: Shadow of Apokolips")_ as well as _[The Batman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Batman\_(TV\_series) "The Batman (TV series)")_ cartoon series. Brown later again played Luthor in the 2009 animated film _[Superman/Batman: Public Enemies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superman/Batman:\_Public\_Enemies "Superman/Batman: Public Enemies")_. He also voiced a character under the name Rohtul (which is Luthor spelled backwards) in _[Batman: Brave and the Bold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batman:\_Brave\_and\_the\_Bold "Batman: Brave and the Bold")_ (while [Kevin Michael Richardson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Michael_Richardson "Kevin Michael Richardson") provided the voice of the actual character). Brown once again voiced Lex in the video games _[Lego Batman 2: DC Super Heroes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lego\_Batman\_2:\_DC\_Super\_Heroes "Lego Batman 2: DC Super Heroes")_, _[Lego Batman 3: Beyond Gotham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lego\_Batman\_3:\_Beyond\_Gotham "Lego Batman 3: Beyond Gotham")_ and _[Lego DC Super-Villains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lego\_DC\_Super-Villains "Lego DC Super-Villains")_. From all these vocal appearances, Brown has played Lex Luthor longer than any other actor in history, including his own _Justice League_ co-star [Michael Rosenbaum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Rosenbaum "Michael Rosenbaum") (in _[Smallville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smallville "Smallville")_).

Brown is also known for his voice work as villains in various [DC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DC_Comics "DC Comics") animated series, films, television shows, and video games: Charlie "Big Time" Bigelow on _[Batman Beyond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batman\_Beyond "Batman Beyond")_, [Trident](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trident_(DC_Comics) "Trident (DC Comics)") on _[Teen Titans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teen\_Titans\_(TV\_series) "Teen Titans (TV series)")_, [Mr. Freeze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr._Freeze "Mr. Freeze") and [Bane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bane_(DC_Comics) "Bane (DC Comics)") on _[The Batman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Batman\_(TV\_series) "The Batman (TV series)")_, [Per Degaton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Per_Degaton "Per Degaton") in _[Batman: The Brave and the Bold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batman:\_The\_Brave\_and\_the\_Bold "Batman: The Brave and the Bold")_, [Parallax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parallax_(character) "Parallax (character)") in the live-action _[Green Lantern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green\_Lantern\_(film) "Green Lantern (film)")_ film, [King Faraday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Faraday "King Faraday") in _[Young Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young\_Justice\_(TV\_series) "Young Justice (TV series)")_, and Zartok in _[Green Lantern: The Animated Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green\_Lantern:\_The\_Animated\_Series "Green Lantern: The Animated Series")_. He appeared on The CW's _[The Flash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Flash\_(2014\_TV\_series) "The Flash (2014 TV series)")_ recurring in the first season as [General Wade Eiling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Wade_Eiling "General Wade Eiling"), and on HBO's _[The Penguin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Penguin\_(TV\_series) "The Penguin (TV series)")_ as [Sal Maroni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sal_Maroni "Sal Maroni").

## Activism

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Clancy_Brown&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Activism")]

On March 30, 2012, the [Screen Actors Guild](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild "Screen Actors Guild") (SAG) and the [American Federation of Television and Radio Artists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Federation_of_Television_and_Radio_Artists "American Federation of Television and Radio Artists") (AFTRA) completed a merger of equals forming a new union [SAG-AFTRA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAG-AFTRA "SAG-AFTRA"). As a result of this merger, a group of actors including Brown, fellow voice actors [Michael Bell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bell_(actor) "Michael Bell (actor)"), [Wendy Schaal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wendy_Schaal "Wendy Schaal"), Schaal's former stepmother [Valerie Harper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valerie_Harper "Valerie Harper"), and other actors including former SAG President [Edward Asner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Asner "Edward Asner"), [Martin Sheen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Sheen "Martin Sheen"), [Ed Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Harris "Ed Harris"), and [Nancy Sinatra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nancy_Sinatra "Nancy Sinatra") immediately sued against the current SAG President [Ken Howard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Howard "Ken Howard") and several SAG Vice Presidents to overturn the merger and separate the (now merged) two unions because of their claims that the election was improper.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clancy_Brown#cite_note-19) The plaintiffs dropped their lawsuit several months later.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clancy_Brown#cite_note-20)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Clancy_Brown&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Brown has been married to Jeanne Johnson since 1993.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clancy_Brown#cite_note-Empire-21) They have two children.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clancy_Brown#cite_note-Empire-21)

Brown is involved in charity organizations, supporting the Beth Brown Memorial Fund named after his late sister, which offers scholarships to students who want to study pediatric healthcare.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clancy_Brown#cite_note-22) In 1999 he spearheaded a charity campaign to support [J. Madison Wright](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._Madison_Wright_Morris "J. Madison Wright Morris"), his on-screen daughter from _Earth 2_, who needed a heart transplant.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clancy_Brown#cite_note-23) He has also given back to his Alma mater the Northwestern University through benefit performances.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clancy_Brown#cite_note-24)

In a 2023 interview with [NPR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NPR "NPR"), Brown said that he came from a "very long legacy of [Republican ideology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)") - back when they _had_ an ideology." His father, Bud Brown, had passed from [COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19") complications the previous year.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clancy_Brown#cite_note-25)

_**Uncharted 3: Drake's Deception**_ is a 2011 [action-adventure game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Action-adventure_game "Action-adventure game") developed by [Naughty Dog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naughty_Dog "Naughty Dog") and published by [Sony Computer Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Computer_Entertainment "Sony Computer Entertainment") for the [PlayStation 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_3 "PlayStation 3"). It is the third main entry in the _[Uncharted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uncharted "Uncharted")_ series. Set two years after _[Among Thieves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uncharted\_2:\_Among\_Thieves "Uncharted 2: Among Thieves")_ (2009), the single-player story follows [Nathan Drake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nathan_Drake "Nathan Drake") and his mentor [Victor Sullivan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Uncharted_characters#Victor_%22Sully%22_Sullivan "List of Uncharted characters") as they search for the legendary [lost city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lost_city "Lost city") of [Iram of the Pillars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iram_of_the_Pillars "Iram of the Pillars") while battling a secret society led by Sullivan's former employer, [Katherine Marlowe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Uncharted_characters#Katherine_Marlowe "List of Uncharted characters").

Development for _Uncharted 3_ began in 2010. Development was approached by incorporating locations distinct from the series' previous entries, with the team deciding on deserts and urban areas, drawing inspiration for the plot from the life of archaeologist [T. E. Lawrence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T._E._Lawrence "T. E. Lawrence"). Naughty Dog sought to upgrade the game's openness and realism, increasing the volume of [motion capture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motion_capture "Motion capture") and voice acting, and conducting field research for better visual environments and sounds. The development team also aimed to improve the multiplayer system, introducing new competitive and co-operative modes, while the game is also notable for being one of the first to carry the new online [PlayStation Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Network "PlayStation Network")[Pass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Online_pass "Online pass") feature.

_Drake's Deception_ received acclaim for its voice acting, graphics, story, and cinematic quality, though some criticized its linearity and found it inferior to its predecessor. The game received [Game of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Game_of_the_Year_awards "List of Game of the Year awards") accolades from numerous publications and award events, and was a commercial success, selling over nine million copies worldwide,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uncharted_3:_Drake's_Deception#cite_note-:0-3) making it one of the [best-selling PlayStation 3 games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best-selling_PlayStation_3_games "Best-selling PlayStation 3 games"). The game was followed by the sequel _[Uncharted 4: A Thief's End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uncharted\_4:\_A\_Thief's\_End "Uncharted 4: A Thief's End")_ in 2016, and was re-released on [PlayStation 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_4 "PlayStation 4") as part of _[Uncharted: The Nathan Drake Collection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uncharted:\_The\_Nathan\_Drake\_Collection "Uncharted: The Nathan Drake Collection")_.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uncharted_3:_Drake's_Deception#cite_note-4)

## Gameplay

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Uncharted_3:_Drake%27s_Deception&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Gameplay")]

_Uncharted 3: Drake's Deception_ is an [action-adventure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Action-adventure_game "Action-adventure game")[platform](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Platform_game "Platform game")[video game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_game "Video game") played from a [third-person perspective](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third-person_perspective "Third-person perspective"), with the player in control of [Nathan Drake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nathan_Drake "Nathan Drake"). Drake has a large number of different animation sets, enabling him to react according to his surroundings. Drake is physically adept and can jump, sprint, climb, swim, scale narrow ledges and wall faces to get between points, and perform other [acrobatic actions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parkour "Parkour"). Drake can now take on opponents in more ways than before: hand-to-hand combat with multiple opponents, contextual melee attacks, and new stealth options. _Uncharted 3_ also features expanded and diverse traversal moves with deep gunplay. Drake can be equipped with up to two firearms – one single-handed and one two-handed – and four grenades. Drake can pick up weapons, automatically replacing the existing weapon he was using, and additional ammunition from downed enemies.

The player can direct Drake to take [cover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cover_system "Cover system") behind corners or low walls using either aimed or blind fire to kill his enemies. The player can also have Drake fire while moving. If Drake is undetected by his enemies, the player can attempt to use stealth to take them out, such as by sneaking up behind them and killing them with one hit, or by dropping down onto an enemy whilst Drake is hanging from a ledge. The stealth mechanic has been simplified and improved.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uncharted_3:_Drake's_Deception#cite_note-gi_reveal-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uncharted_3:_Drake's_Deception#cite_note-6) Some areas of the game will require the player to solve puzzles with the use of Drake's journal, which provides clues towards the puzzles' solutions. When enabled, a hint system provides gameplay clues, such as the direction of the next objective.

### Multiplayer

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Uncharted_3:_Drake%27s_Deception&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Multiplayer")]

Similarly to _[Uncharted 2: Among Thieves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uncharted\_2:\_Among\_Thieves "Uncharted 2: Among Thieves")_, _Uncharted 3_ includes a separate multiplayer component with network play, featuring competitive and [co-operative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cooperative_video_game "Cooperative video game") modes of play. The beta features several customization options, such as different character skins, clown masks, ability boosters, skill medals to attain, and a progressive ranking system. _Uncharted 3_ will introduce free-for-all modes such as standard deathmatch, character model and weapon modification, and dynamic environmental 'events' within multiplayer maps, similar to the set pieces from the game's campaign – such as a hostile plane flying above shooting all players it catches in its crossfire. Collectible treasures are also said to be available within the multiplayer maps, which can be used as in-game currency for unlocking new characters, customization equipment, and boosters. Unlocked customizations can either allow for changes to be made in character appearances, such as clothing and skin tone or upgrade weapon attributes.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

A Buddy System has also been implemented into multiplayer. At the beginning of each match, the player may be joined by a random partner or a friend if joining their game. The buddy's emblem remains displayed as part of the player's HUD to indicate their location relative to the player's own on the map. With your Buddy, you can do a cooperative taunt over dead enemies you defeated together, and can also collect each other's earned treasures for them. The player can spawn next to his buddy so long as the buddy remains alive and out of combat.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] With the aim of making the multiplayer more flexible and accessible, several logistical improvements have been added, such as the capability to join games in progress or for two different [PlayStation Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_Network "PlayStation Network") accounts to play together in split-screen multiplayer on a single console. In the event of ties or near-ties, matches enter an elimination mode as they wind down, in which the players are restricted to one life and must compete to wipe out all of the opposing team's members first within the allotted remaining time.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Several new features have been included in the game, including mechanics that create gameplay situations designed to assist the losing team, improves ability enhancements and augmentations that must be purchased for each use, special abilities that are made available when a certain number of medals has been attained within a match, and "Uncharted TV", a small video window that appears throughout the multiplayer menus, creating a video that can be uploaded to [Facebook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facebook "Facebook"), [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") or the [XMB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XMB "XMB"). Multiplayer also includes a [character creation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Character_creation "Character creation") system, allowing a user to extensively customize their in-game character. Cooperative multiplayer also returns from _Uncharted 2_.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The multiplayer servers of _Uncharted 3: Drake's Deception_ were terminated on September 3, 2019, along with its predecessor as well.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uncharted_3:_Drake's_Deception#cite_note-7)
